tool_input.prompt: Current minor versions for each major (esp. 16.x, 18.x), release dates, EOL dates. Today's date context 2026-11-01.

tool_result_content:
As of 2026-11-01, these are the supported PostgreSQL branches:

| Major | Current minor | First release | Final release (EOL) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18 | 18.6 | Sep 25, 2025 | Nov 14, 2030 | Supported |
| 17 | 17.11 | Sep 26, 2024 | Nov 8, 2029 | Supported |
| 16 | 16.15 | Sep 14, 2023 | Nov 9, 2028 | Supported |
| 15 | 15.19 | Oct 13, 2022 | Nov 11, 2027 | Supported |
| 14 | 14.24 | Sep 30, 2021 | Nov 12, 2026 | Supported, EOL in about 11 days |

Majors 13 and older are unsupported. The most recent was 13, which reached EOL on Nov 13, 2025.

Key points from the policy:
- Each major is supported for 5 years after its initial release.
- Minor releases with bug and security fixes come at least once every three months.
- Minor upgrades don't need a dump and restore. Stop the server, install the new binaries, and restart. Always read the release notes first.
- Major upgrades require `pg_upgrade` or a dump/reload.
- The PostgreSQL project recommends always running the current minor release of your major version.

PostgreSQL 14 users should plan a major upgrade before November 12, 2026. The page also announces PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 (released October 15, 2026), which isn't in the table yet.
